reasons: Both answers correct the company at the start on both premises: 14 days under Article 9(1), and an extension only with mutual agreement. Both give a plausible severance figure of about 10.2 to 10.4 million won. B adds the ordinary-wage floor (about 126,316 won a day, so about 12 million won), which changes the answer by roughly 1.8 million won and is the main content gap in A. B also names the labor-portal complaint, 1350 and the local labor office, and it tells the user to check the payslip and which basis the company used. A is better on three points: it gives the current penalty (5 years or 50 million won under Article 43) where B cites the old Article 44 (3 years or 30 million won); its message is firm, says outright that the user never agreed to an extension, and carries no threat; and it is shorter. B's message version 1 has a mild threat and a 'will discuss' phrasing, and B overall is longer, with two message versions. B wins slightly because of the ordinary-wage floor and the complaint and 1350 guidance.
